Forcing a migration to an incompatible version throws away GA's install-base moat: switching tools breaks historical comparisons, so if history is lost anyway there is less reason to stay. GA4's completely different data model also undermines the many BI tool plug-ins built for Universal Analytics.

GA4 feels like a huge step backwards. Lots of functionality from the previous version is missing or replaced with smart 'insights', where you describe your query in plain text and it always gets it wrong.
For many users GA4 hides the number one metric they look for: 'pageviews' are now an event called 'page_view'. Event-driven tracking makes sense for SPAs, but Google will lose some users over this.
A 12-step upgrade procedure is insane. I have an extremely basic setup that took 5 minutes to start using. Why is this not a one-click upgrade?

I hate everything about GA4: a counter-intuitive, massively over-complex interface. Things that were easy in the old version are now insanely hard or missing. I'm moving my clients to Matomo and they're loving it.
As a hobbyist, I'll lose the data from the day my blog hit the HN front page. I wish UA data could be migrated to GA4, but it doesn't seem possible.

Nothing else gives the same integration between SEO and PPC. Building a GA-based custom audience (device, pages visited, events, location) for AdWords campaigns, or using Optimize for PPC, requires GA. It's out of the box and free, versus needing multiple vendors. That's the Google lock-in.
Most SaaS reporting tools lacked GA4 integrations when I last checked. We've been running both UA and GA4 via separate gtag('config') lines for some time in anticipation of the switch.

GA became so complicated over the years that it was hard to act on the results. After switching to Plausible for data protection reasons, I suddenly understood every metric and use analytics far more for decision-making.
I have tried GA4, but the issue with events not being recorded still hasn't been fixed.

It's rare that an interface makes me feel as dumb and frustrated as GA4. The user report offers 'today' and 'yesterday' even though processing can take up to 48 hours, so 'today' always shows zero users. Real-time reporting works reasonably well but is limited to a 30-minute window.

GA4 is clearly aimed at data scientists. Even as someone who owns data teams, it's frustrating to use. Count the steps needed to get a page's view count in Universal Analytics versus GA4, if you can even figure out how in GA4.

Historical GA data will not be viewable in your GA4 property. The biggest moat, years of page-view data for trend comparisons, is broken. The forced migration is handled so badly it seems Google would rather nobody use GA.
I recently gave GA4 a shot and felt I had more access to information, and better analytics, in 1998. It's a disaster.

We switched our non-profit Drupal clients from GA to Plausible because of GA4. It's not free, but cheap enough that they'll pay to avoid the hassle. It has a simple interface and we embed the dashboard in the Drupal admin.

Defense of GA4: it's hit-based and takes GDPR into account. It hooks into BigQuery easily (a few bucks a month), which feeds Looker Studio, and it's free. You can personalize the main menu, remove e-commerce if unused, and build custom reports in 'Explore'. You do have to learn the new interface.
I'm frustrated with GA, but one thing it does very well that I can't find elsewhere is counting unique unregistered visitors.
The only thing keeping me from immediately jumping ship from GA is that it's free.

The GA4 interface, along with Ads and some Cloud interfaces, is so bizarrely complex it's comical. It could take my team a week to find the page something was on or decipher the convoluted naming scheme.
GA4 is not ready for prime time. Many alternatives count data differently than GA, so run an alternative alongside GA first to avoid being surprised by an apparent drop in visitors.
